headline: Discussed Lake Street traffic calming, solid waste tax structure, and wastewater treatment plant project update.
summary: The committee heard presentations on Lake Street traffic calming concerns, the solid waste generation tax and flow control structure, and an update on the Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvement Project. Councilors asked questions and raised concerns on each topic, but no formal votes were taken on these items. The director gave updates on Main Street, unaccepted streets, and paving, and councilors raised items for future reports.

Chair Barlow calls the meeting to order at 5:30 pm. 
Councilor McKnight opened the meeting by expressing condolences to the family of Shiloh 
Skalka, who died in a bicycle accident near the meeting location, and encouraged attendees to 
reflect on how the community can make Burlington safer for children 
1. Agenda 
Councilor Bergman moves to adopt the agenda as posted on civic clerk. 
Councilor Broderick seconds. 
All in favor, Unanimous approval   
 
2. Minutes of 6/23/26 
Councilor Bergman moves to adopt the minutes as posted. 
Councilor Broderick seconds.  
All in favor, Unanimous approval 
 
3. Public Forum 
Sharon Bushor – Former City Councilor and resident of Burlington - raised concerns 
about the solid waste tax and recycling funding, highlighting alternative practices like taking 
waste to drop-off sites and combining recycling efforts among small households, and 
requested more information about how funding works with the Solid Waste District. 
4. Deliberative Agenda 
 4.1 Lake Street Traffic Calming  
Robert Sand – Ward 3 presented information.
Councilor Bergman asked about timing and relation with Police Dept.  Councilor McKnight 
asked does the city have a cross department task force?  Councilor Broderick said same 
issue on College St.  Chair Barlow asked what time of day? Does it start at a certain time? 
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions: The meeting focused on a Lake Street 
traffic calming resolution passed by the Ward 3 MPA, with Robert Sanders presenting 
concerns about dangerous motorcycle speeds and lack of enforcement in the waterfront 
corridor. Chapin Spencer, Director of Public Works, acknowledged existing traffic calming 
measures on Lake Street have not achieved desired outcomes and noted the department's 
limited capacity to address enforcement gaps. The discussion highlighted the need for better 
coordination between DPW and the police department, with Councilor McKnight suggesting 
the formation of a cross-departmental task force to address enforcement and education 
challenges. 
4.2 Solid Waste Generation Tax Flow Control & Tax Structure  
Lee Perry, Assistant Director Maintenance & ROW provided information. 
 
Councilor Bergman asked about Drop off Center Customers? Feels we should explore the 
affordability programs. Councilor Broderick agrees with Councilor Bergman and to make 
sure we are charging tax to everyone that lives in the City. Also asked about the tier system. 
Chair Barlow has the same concerns about how to capture the self-haulers. 
 
Sharon Bushor commented that the South Burlington drop of center was asking for your zip 
code. 
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions:  The group discussed concerns about 
capturing Burlington residents who self-haul waste to South Burlington drop-off centers, as 
they may pay lower fees than if collected by a hauler. DPW raised the issue of ensuring proper 
residency verification at drop-off centers, though this would create operational challenges for 
CSWD. The discussion included exploring affordability programs and potential solutions like 
zip code tracking, with the group agreeing to further discuss these issues with CSWD and 
consider long-term approaches to consolidated collection. 
 4.3   Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvement Project Update 
Martin Lee, Water Resources Engineering Manager presented information. 
 
Councilor Bergman asked what is the worst-case scenario?  What would be the collateral 
impacts of that, and what is our contingency planning for that?    Chair Barlow do you have 
more than one proposal? 
AI generated minutes w/ slight staff revisions: Martin Lee provided a comprehensive 
update on the Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvement Project, highlighting the current 
Stage Zero construction and plans for Stage 1 improvements. The project, approved in 2025 
with an estimated cost of $127 million, aims to enhance capacity, improve phosphorus 
treatment, and address aging infrastructure. Key stakeholders include Parks and Recreation, 
Burlington Electric Department, and the State, with coordination ongoing regarding parking, 
electrical lines, and bike path impacts. The team plans to engage a construction manager at 
risk (CMAR) and will seek approval for the engineer's contract through 100% final design.
5. Director’s Report 
 
• We’re excited for the successful celebration for Main St – Every Department & 
Division was involved.  Lower Church St – still finishing up sidewalk work.  B.E.D is 
fixing a defect on some of the poles. 
• Unaccepted Streets - Coming soon with suggested grouping. 
• Paving a series of North End Streets in the next few weeks. 
 
 
6. Councilor Items 
Councilor Bergman – Loved the Main St opening celebration.  Who is watering the trees?  
Protected bike lanes on Elmwood Ave after Grant St– tree that spreads out, who’s 
responsibility is it?  Request a future report on the traffic data on Maple & Pine and King & 
Pine and the issues to left hand turn lanes.  
Councilor Broderick – College St & Willard St great job with getting pedestrian signals up.   
Chair Barlow – Maple St & King St data - smart lights active? Lots of appreciation to the New 
North End for new sidewalks. 
 
7. Next Meeting 
August 25, 2026, 5:30 pm at 645 Pine St. 
 
8. Adjournment 
Chair Barlow adjourns meeting  7:05 pm.
